ownership: Root proposed the quantified consequence of1234 and1248. bounded_idea_supply checked the arbitrary-code argument, the first-head issue and the old active_groups implementation. No native payload, recount, new solver or GDT was used.
contract: A fixed prefix-free set C of distinct nonempty strings over the unchanged22 working units covers every unchanged1233 complete whole group in one reader. The total table has at most31 entries; arbitrary finite code lengths are allowed. The statement concerns segmentation into code entries, not assigned source letters or meanings. Original whole-group boundaries and exact working-unit parsing are retained.

inherited_obligations.all_heads: All22 working signs begin some complete remainder in the valid left-quotient closure R. Each therefore requires at least one code entry with that first sign.
inherited_obligations.second_sign_branch_counts: cfh and cph each have six distinct second signs in complete remainders. A non-singleton code with either head therefore needs at least six distinct entries with that head. q needs at least11 such entries in IT/ZL and12 in RF.
inherited_obligations.scope: These are retained exact full-panel conclusions, including their rare-reading premises, not new empirical measurements or unconditional facts about a native alphabet.

proof_head_restriction: If a singleton sign g belongs to a prefix-free C, no longer code may start with g. The19forced singleton signs therefore cannot head any longer code, at any table size.
For a non-singleton q head, at least21 other head entries plus11 IT/ZL or12 RF q entries are necessary: total at least32 or33. Thus a table of at most31 entries must contain singleton q.

If both cfh and cph are non-singleton heads, their entries are disjoint by first sign. At least20 entries for the other heads plus6 cfh entries plus6 cph entries are required:32. This is excluded at the proposed cap31.

Consequently a complete table of at most31 entries is either the22-singleton identity table, or has exactly one non-singleton head h in {cfh,cph}. Every other one of the21 working units is a singleton code.

In the nontrivial case every longer code starts with the selected h. The h-codes may have arbitrary finite lengths and may themselves contain further h units. The proof does not assume the two-unit construction of1248, exactly27 entries, or a bound on codeword length.
proof_group_activity: Call a whole group active when its unique complete C-parse uses at least one code longer than one working unit.
If a group contains no selected h, it cannot use a longer code, because every longer code starts with h. Every unit of that group is parsed as a singleton.

If a group contains h, consider its FIRST occurrence. All preceding units are different from h and have singleton codes; no longer code can start among them. Hence decoding reaches this first h at a code boundary. Since h is not itself a singleton, a longer h-headed code must begin there.

A later h may be swallowed inside that longer code, and several h occurrences may be covered together. This does not defeat activity: the group already contains at least one longer code. Thus for every complete table in the nontrivial case, active(group) is EXACTLY the predicate 'group contains h'.
The quantifier is over every complete prefix-free table of at most31 entries, not merely1248's two pair tables. A table cannot combine the two rare-head activity sets at that size.

transfer_of_old_counts.implementation_meaning: The old parser takes each non-h sign alone and h with the next unit. It scans the entire group. active_groups increments by any(len(code)>1 for code in pieces), once per accepted occurrence. It is not an initial-position count or a number of distinct word types. Every reported cfh/cph case has zero failures.
transfer_of_old_counts.why_no_new_census_is_needed_for_this_tra: For that fully covering pair parser, the same first-h argument proves active_groups equals the number of original group occurrences containing h anywhere. Therefore those already reported counts are the exact group-activity counts for every new complete table with that selected h, even if its h entries are longer than two units. Multiple h occurrences or h inside a long code do not change this equality.
transfer_of_old_counts.identity_case: If C is the singleton identity table, its active count is zero. The displayed uniform bounds include this case.
transfer_of_old_counts.provenance: Numbers and shares are copied from the old published1248report and interpreted through its read-only source code. This review did not open GROUPS, count occurrences or independently rerun the old numerical validation.

rare_form_dependency.retained: The full19-singleton/27-entry result depends on rare complete forms. On the predeclared recurrent-type subset, the same method forced15singletons in IT/RF and14 in ZL, with necessary bound23. In the full quotient proof system, ckh,cth,f,i require a one-token source type in every reader, with ch additionally so in ZL.
rare_form_dependency.consequence: The present universal<=31 activity restriction inherits the full-panel proof. It is not an error-tolerant or recurrent-only theorem. Removing exceptional forms or changing the working alphabet would change the premise; no such removal or repair is adopted.
rare_form_dependency.not_claimed: The review does not claim those rare forms are errors, that these are the only possible forcing arguments, or that an error budget would yield a successful different table.

limits: Group activity is not the fraction of glyphs changed or the number of long-code occurrences. One rare-head group could contain a long code covering many other signs. No glyph-activity or length-reduction bound is inferred here.
No H2/entropy decrease is quantified. A small active-group fraction alone supplies no numerical conditional-entropy effect, and no source alphabet or fixed source text is decoded by this result.
Singleton segmentation does not mean native language content is known or uninteresting; its source-letter labels, vocabulary and meanings remain unassigned.
The population is the old strict-interior literal P-group panel, not every native group, label, margin or complete message. Alternate readers remain separate readings of the same manuscript.

The theorem requires free prefix parsing of each complete group. General non-prefix UD, grammar-conditioned codes, contextual spellings, changed units or cross-space codes are different contracts and retain their separate outcomes.

The cap31 is the threshold of this formal corollary, not an independently established historical alphabet size. The conclusion does not authorize an automatic32-entry decoder or new head/table optimization.

The old27-entry attainability PASS remains true. This result clarifies that its tiny affected-group share extends to every complete table through31 entries under the same exact assumptions; it neither invalidates that formal construction nor promotes it as a practical reading.
